title: Convergent and Divergent Neural Signatures of Cue-Induced Response in Substance and Behavioral Addictions: A Coordinate-Based Neuroimaging Meta-Analysis
title_zh: 物质和行为成瘾中线索诱导反应的融合与发散神经标志物：基于坐标的神经影像学元分析
abstract: Addiction-related cues trigger craving and precipitate relapse, yet whether substance use disorders (SUDs) and behavioral addictions (BAs) share a universal neurobiological cue-reactivity core remains unresolved. We conducted a coordinate-based meta-analysis using Seed-based d Mapping with Permutation of Subject Images (SDM-PSI) to synthesize whole-brain fMRI studies comparing visually evoked cue-reactivity in strictly diagnosed SUDs and BAs versus healthy controls. An updated systematic search through September 12, 2026, yielded 50 eligible articles comprising 53 independent contrasts and 2,578 participants. Pooled analyses across all addictions revealed convergent cue-elicited activations in the mid-cingulate cortex, precentral gyrus, and a midline midbrain region. However, a formal SUD ∩ BA conjunction analysis yielded no family-wise error (FWE)-corrected shared clusters. Direct comparisons demonstrated greater activation in the left hippocampus, pregenual anterior cingulate cortex, and precuneus for SUDs relative to BAs. Importantly, the left hippocampal and precuneus differences survived age adjustment; furthermore, the hippocampal finding remained robust when restricting analyses to highly controlled cue-versus-neutral paradigms, while the precuneus finding was retained within picture-cue modalities. Furthermore, exploratory analyses of clinical characteristics indicated that cue-elicited neural responses were associated with specific clinical states and treatment variables (e.g., methadone maintenance in heroin use disorder), highlighting the modulatory effect of clinical symptom profiles on these regional functional signatures. Overall, the results motivate further investigation of memory- and self-related processes, as well as control- or action-related processes. These findings offer a critical foundation for developing targeted clinical interventions, distinguishing between generalized transdiagnostic neuromodulation targets and disorder-specific therapies tailored to distinct clinical and demographic profile.
abstract_zh: 与成瘾相关的线索会引发渴望并诱发复发，但物质使用障碍（SUDs）和行为成瘾（BAs）是否共享一个普遍的线索反应性神经生物学核心仍未解明。我们利用种子映射-主体图像置换（SDM-PSI）进行坐标基础元分析，综合了全脑 fMRI 研究，比较了严格诊断的 SUDs 和 BAs 与健康对照组之间视觉诱发的线索反应性。截至 2026 年 9 月 12 日的更新系统检索筛选出 50 篇合格文章，包含 53 个独立对比和 2578 名参与者。所有成瘾类型的合并分析显示，在前中回、中央前回以及一条中线中脑区域出现收敛的线索诱发激活。然而，正式的 SUD ∩ BA 重合分析未发现经家系误差（FWE）校正的共享聚类。直接比较显示，SUDs 相对于 BAs，左侧海马、前膝前扣带回皮层和楔前叶激活更明显。重要的是，左侧海马和楔前叶的差异经年龄调整后仍然存在；此外，当将分析限制在高度控制的线索对照范式时，海马发现仍然稳健，而楔前叶发现则在图片线索模式中保留。进一步，探索性临床特征分析表明，线索诱发的神经反应与特定临床状态和治疗变量（例如海洛因使用障碍的美沙酮维持治疗）相关，突显了临床症状特征对这些区域性功能标志物的调节作用。总体而言，结果推动了对记忆和自我相关过程，以及控制或动作相关过程的进一步研究。这些发现为开发针对性临床干预措施提供了关键基础，以区分通用跨诊断神经调节靶点与针对特定临床和人口统计特征的疾病特异性治疗。
